segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ אַנְשֵׁי חָצֵר וְאַנְשֵׁי מִרְפֶּסֶת שֶׁשָּׁכְחוּ וְלֹא עֵירְבוּ, כׇּל שֶׁגָּבוֹהַּ עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים — לְמִרְפֶּסֶת. פָּחוֹת מִכָּאן — לֶחָצֵר.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» If both «the residents of» houses that open directly into «a courtyard and the residents of» apartments that open onto «a balcony» from which stairs lead down to that courtyard «forgot and did not establish an eiruv» between them, «anything» in the courtyard «that is ten handbreadths high,» e.g., a mound or a post, is part «of the balcony.» The residents of the apartments open to the balcony may transfer objects to and from their apartments onto the mound or post. Any post or mound that is «lower than this» height is part «of the courtyard.»

segments.he: חוּלְיַית הַבּוֹר וְהַסֶּלַע, גְּבוֹהִים עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים — לַמִּרְפֶּסֶת, פָּחוֹת מִכָּאן — לֶחָצֵר.
segments.en: A similar halakha applies to «an embankment» that surrounds «a cistern or a rock:» If the embankments that surround a cistern or rock are «ten handbreadths high,» they belong «to the balcony;» if they are «lower than this,» they may be used only «by» the inhabitants of «the courtyard.»

segments.he: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים — בִּסְמוּכָה, אֲבָל בְּמוּפְלֶגֶת — אֲפִילּוּ גָּבוֹהַּ עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים — לֶחָצֵר. וְאֵיזוֹ הִיא סְמוּכָה — כׇּל שֶׁאֵינָהּ רְחוֹקָה אַרְבָּעָה טְפָחִים.
segments.en: «In what» case «are these matters,» the halakha that anything higher than ten handbreadths belongs to the balcony, «stated?» When the mound or embankment is «near» the balcony. «But in» a case where the embankment or mound is «distant» from it, «even» if it is «ten handbreadths high,» the right to use the embankment or mound goes «to» the members of «the courtyard. And what is» considered «near? Anything that is not four handbreadths removed» from the balcony.

moves.cueHe: אנשי חצר ואנשי מרפסת ששכחו ולא עירבו
moves.summary: Ten-handbreadth objects go to the balcony, lower ones to the courtyard
Same for a cistern embankment or a rock
Only when near the balcony; if distant, it belongs to the courtyard

positions.claim: anything ten handbreadths high belongs to the balcony, lower to the courtyard, provided it is within four handbreadths of the balcony
